newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon's BLC bank 1996 profits up 194 pct.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon's BLC bank 1996 profits up 194 pct.

text.p: Banque Libanaise pour le Commerce said on Friday pre-tax profits rose 194 percent in 1996 to $9.54 million from $3.25 million in 1995.
Total assets rose 30 percent according to highlights of the bank's unaudited consolidated results issued on Friday.
BLC, which ranked 13th among Lebanon's 82 banks in customer deposits in 1995, in December became the first Lebanese bank to list shares on the Beirut Stock Exchange.

Last December, BLC completed a $60 million capital increase through simultaneous local and international share offerings.
It said the increase would cover acquisition of BLC France, its Paris subsidiary which split off during the 1975-1990 civil war and has four branches in the United Arab Emirates.

"With the capital increase that took place at end 1996 and the considation of the Bank's operations in Lebanon and overseas, BLC is well positioned to achieve its growth and profitability targets for 1997," BLC said in a statement.
